chunks: From what was narrated by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ṣafwān, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating. He said: “He should not seek to do that, for Allah has forbidden that he approach her.” I said: “If he did so, is there any kaffarah upon him?” He said: “I do not know of anything concerning it; he should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.”
And similarly what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Abī Jamīlah, from Layth al-Murādī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man falling upon his wife while she was menstruating by mistake. He said: “There is nothing upon him, though he has disobeyed his Lord.”

key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: an expiatory penalty due for a prohibited act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intercourse during menstruation, and is kaffarah required?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on intercourse with a menstruating wife and states that such an act is prohibited. It indicates that no specific kaffarah is known in this report, and that one should seek forgiveness from Allah, while another version states that nothing is due upon the person in the case of mistake.
